subject: Routing policy question: 'lockstep' regional-only serving for TheraHealth
messages:
From: Claire Moss <claire@therahealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production serving request: EU-only + no fallback + pinned model

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We need to move from pilot to production for a customer-facing feature, but our legal/compliance team has mandated two constraints that are blocking sign-off:

1) All inference for TheraHealth customer data must be served from EU-only capacity (data residency).
2) No automatic fallback to any non-EU or lower-tier model variants is allowed (i.e., explicit failure if the requested regional capacity is unavailable).
3) The model variant must be a specific audited quantized build we validated (v2-q8). No automatic model substitution.

Can Redwood support a "lockstep" routing policy that enforces (1)-(3) at the request-routing layer? If possible we need a short mutual action plan + timeline (2–3 weeks target). Attaching our compliance summary and the dataflow diagram for context.

Claire Moss
Product Security Lead, TheraHealth
TheraHealth Inc.
Attachment: TheraHealth_DataFlow.pdf

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 09:05:23 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Production serving request: EU-only + no fallback + pinned model

Looping you all in — TheraHealth is asking for an operational "lockstep" policy: strict EU-only routing, hard no-fallback (fail closed), and a pinned audited variant (v2-q8).

Questions / asks:
- Karthik: is there a safe product path to support a hard no-fallback route and enforce model pinning at the routing layer (short of bespoke infra)?
- Jonas: does security/legal see immediate blocking risk we should escalate?
- Grace/Marcus: operational impact (capacity reservation, SLO changes, monitoring/alerts)?

Claire wants an estimated timeline and a mutual action plan (2–3 weeks target). I expect this to affect Dedicated/Private customers first, but need to understand if Hosted can offer a per-customer lock.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 19, 2028 at 08:12 AM Claire Moss <claire@therahealth.com> wrote:
> Can Redwood support a "lockstep" routing policy that enforces (1)-(3) at the request-routing layer?

Short answer: technically yes, but non-trivial. Notes:

- EU-only routing: we already support region pins per-customer (hosted + dedicated) but it's typically a "preferred" route with fallback. Converting to a hard region enforcement (fail if no EU capacity) is a configuration change + validation to ensure customers understand failure mode.
- No-fallback: we do have a "no auto-fallback" flag used in a couple of enterprise pilots. Implementing it across the stack means disabling the multi-variant routing policy, and ensuring the control plane returns an explicit 503/ROUTE_LOCK when EU capacity is exhausted.
- Model pinning: we can pin to a specific model artifact (model repo + quantization tag). The tricky part is pinning to a build we haven't fully certified on all EU fleets — need model onboarding and kernel compatibility checks.

Estimated effort for a hardened offering (safe for production):
- Short path (sprint-level): enable per-account routing flags + no-fallback enforcement in control plane + ops runbook — 7–10 business days if we divert a small cross-functional team.
- Medium path (sustainable): formal model onboarding for v2-q8 across EU fleet + QA + rollout gating — 3–4 weeks.

I'll volunteer to draft the minimal API/route schema and the rollback semantics. Need ops and security sign-off before we promise Claire a firm timeline.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 11:39:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production serving request: EU-only + no fallback + pinned model

We ran a quick ops impact scan: attaching a small matrix. Immediate highlights:

- Capacity: a hard EU-only + no-fallback constraint increases risk of throttled requests during peak; we'd need either reserved Dedicated capacity or quota-based rate limiting with clear client-side error behavior.
- SLO/Alerting: we must add specific alerts for ROUTE_LOCK failures and ensure CS/AM receive real-time notifications for TheraHealth.
- Deployment: pinning to v2-q8 means we must validate quantization kernels for our EU instance types (A100 vs H100 differences). If kernels fail, requests must surface failure early rather than silently falling back.

Suggested short-term plan (operations):
1) Stand up a reserved EU pool (small) for TheraHealth — ops provisioning 2 business days if capacity available.
2) Add a per-account flag `enforce_regional_lock` and `enforce_model_pin` to the control plane — implementation 3–4 days with mocks.
3) Document client errors and an SDK change that surfaces ROUTE_LOCK (return codes + retry guidance).

Attachment: ops-impact-matrix.csv

Grace O'Connor
Head of Production Operations, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2028 13:42:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production serving request: EU-only + no fallback + pinned model

Thanks for the context. Security take: we can support the policy but require three gating items before production sign-off:

1) Formal attestation from model team that v2-q8 has the same inference semantics as upstream (no silent behavior changes). That includes a checksumed artifact and a signing key.
2) Audit-level request tracing for every inference call tied to TheraHealth's account id (to prove locality + variant). We'll need to extend the tracing retention for this customer for 90 days.
3) Legal to sign an SLA addendum acknowledging the fail-closed behavior (i.e., Redwood will not route outside EU and will return explicit failure when EU capacity low).

Workaround for short-term demo: we can do a canary/private Dedicated with reserved capacity and enhanced logging — that meets Claire's ask with minimal infra changes. For the 2–3 week prod timeline: product + ops to own the control-plane feature, security will iterate on the attestation checklist.

I'll schedule a short review with Legal and Model Ops. Marcus, can you coordinate the model artifact signing?

Jonas Weber
Director, Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
